memories.content: Use the same term throughout the proposal for the same interaction concept or interface element.
Use abbreviations only for recurring terms of three or more words.
Present the full name and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Prioritize the research role over diagnostic labels or deficits when referring to participants.
Reviewers from different subfields struggle to infer undefined abbreviations from context alone.
Use the term formative evaluation for studies seeking design modification evidence, and distinguish it from final efficacy judgments.
The user can have contribution labels such as principles, models, or guidelines approved only if they align with the abstraction level of the actual deliverables.
Design principles describe the relationship between conditions and outcomes rather than serving as instructions that merely replicate a single screen layout.
Specify in one sentence the user population and actual usage environment to which the design knowledge applies.
Reviewers judge the generalization boundary of results through the specified target population and environment.
Specify the workflow, technical infrastructure, and operational-authority conditions that must match before applying the design guidelines at another field site.
The transferability of field design knowledge depends not only on user characteristics but also on workflow and technological–organizational infrastructure.
The user tends to apply results confirmed at one deployment site to all similar organizations.

analysis.overview: The frames address complementary proposal-quality concerns without making overlapping operational claims. The reference frame governs terminology, abbreviations, participant language, evaluation framing, and contribution labeling; the compared frame governs generalization boundaries, transfer conditions, and overextension from single-site evidence.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only rule about terminological consistency, with no counterpart governing the same decision in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Use consistent terminology for each interaction concept or interface element throughout a proposal.

relations.reason: This reference-only rule determines when abbreviation is appropriate; the compared frame contains no corresponding abbreviation policy.
relations.summary: Reserve abbreviations for recurring terms containing at least three words.

relations.reason: The reference memories express the instruction and its reviewer-comprehension rationale as one underlying first-use abbreviation claim, absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Introduce an abbreviation alongside its full name because reviewers cannot reliably infer undefined abbreviations.

relations.reason: This is a standalone reference-only policy for participant language and is not addressed by the compared frame.
relations.summary: Refer to participants by prioritizing their research role over diagnoses or perceived deficits.

relations.reason: This reference-only terminology rule governs evaluation framing, whereas the compared frame addresses applicability boundaries.
relations.summary: Call design-modification studies formative evaluations and distinguish them from final efficacy judgments.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only rule for selecting contribution labels, without a same-decision counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Use contribution labels such as principles, models, or guidelines only when their abstraction matches the actual deliverables.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim defines the proper abstraction and function of design principles; transfer conditions in the compared frame do not govern that definition.
relations.summary: Treat design principles as condition–outcome relationships rather than instructions reproducing one screen layout.

relations.reason: The compared memories provide an instruction and its review rationale for one underlying applicability-boundary claim, which the reference frame does not address.
relations.summary: State the applicable user population and usage environment so reviewers can identify the results’ generalization boundary.

relations.reason: The compared memories jointly state that transferability depends on operational and technological–organizational conditions beyond user characteristics; no reference memory governs this transfer decision.
relations.summary: Specify matching workflow, technical infrastructure, and organizational authority conditions before transferring design guidelines to another site.

relations.reason: This is a compared-only observation about a specific generalization risk and is independently useful from the prescriptions defining applicability and transfer conditions.
relations.summary: Results confirmed at one deployment site tend to be overgeneralized to all similar organizations.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame requires explicit population, environment, workflow, infrastructure, and authority boundaries for transfer, while noting the risk of overgeneralizing single-site results.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers consistent terminology, disciplined abbreviation use, participant-respectful language, formative evaluation, and contribution labels matched to deliverable abstraction.
